# OpenMatthew

> Unofficial, community project. Not affiliated with Chiang Mai University or the Matthew AI team. Use your own CMU account at your own risk.

Use your CMU [Matthew AI](https://matthew.cmu.ac.th) account from any app that speaks the OpenAI API. OpenMatthew runs on your computer and translates between the two.

## Quick start

You need Node.js 20 or newer, and git.

1. Get the code and install it:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/ChindanaiNaKub/OpenMatthew
   cd OpenMatthew
   npm install
   ```

2. Start the server. Leave this terminal open:

   ```bash
   npm run serve
   ```

3. In a second terminal, get your token:

   ```bash
   npm run creds
   ```

   Log in at [matthew.cmu.ac.th](https://matthew.cmu.ac.th). Press `F12`, open the **Console** tab, and run `copy(localStorage.user)`. Paste the result into the terminal and press Enter. Copy the token it prints.

4. In your app, set:

   | Setting | Value |
   |---------|-------|
   | Base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:4141/v1` |
   | API key | the token from step 3 |
   | Model | `gpt-6.1-sol` |

The token logs in as you. Keep it private, and do not paste it into an AI chat.

## Let an AI agent do the setup

Paste this into a coding agent. It stops before the token step, so your token stays with you:

```
Set up OpenMatthew on this computer. Repo: https://github.com/ChindanaiNaKub/OpenMatthew

1. Clone it, run `npm install`, then start `npm run serve` in the background.
2. Check that http://127.0.0.1:4141/v1/models returns a JSON model list.
3. Stop there. Tell me to run `npm run creds` myself. Do not ask me to paste my token into this chat.
```

## Connect your app

- **Any OpenAI-compatible app:** use the settings in step 4 above.
- **Hermes Agent:** in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, set `provider: custom`, `base_url: http://127.0.0.1:4141/v1`, and your token as `api_key`.

## Images

`POST /v1/images/generations` returns an image URL, or base64 with `"response_format": "b64_json"`:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:4141/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "a red apple on a white background"}'
```

- Your default assistant must have **Image generation (GPT-Image-2.5)** on. Otherwise the server returns a 502.
- Matthew allows 15 images per day. Each call counts.
- Only `n: 1` is supported. `size` and `model` are ignored.

## Models

These are the model ids Matthew ships:

| Model | Reasoning |
|-------|-----------|
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | Yes. Newest flagship. |
| `gpt-6-sol` | Yes |
| `gpt-6-luna` | No. Fast and efficient. |
| `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5-mini` | Yes |
| `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini` | No |

Matthew ignores the model you request. Your default assistant answers every request. Change the assistant on matthew.cmu.ac.th.

## Limits

- **The OpenCode plugin targets OpenCode v2.** It runs on `@opencode/plugin`. Older OpenCode v1 releases do not load it.
- **Tool calls are emulated.** The server writes tool schemas into the prompt and parses the reply. It is less reliable than a native tool API.
- **Matthew's API is undocumented.** When something breaks, run `npm run check-api`. It reads Matthew's own frontend bundle and reports changed assumptions.

## Configuration

All optional.

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `PORT` | Server port (default `4141`) |
| `MATTHEW_API_BASE` | Override the Matthew API base URL |

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm test           # unit tests, no network needed
npm run build
npm run check-api  # check the live API for drift (needs network)
```

# Changelog

## Unreleased

### Added

- **Tool calling**, emulated over an API that has none. Matthew takes a
  string and returns a string, so the schemas from a request's `tools` are
  rendered into the prompt, the model is asked to answer in a `<tool_call>`
  protocol, and that is parsed back into OpenAI `tool_calls` with
  `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. Covers `tool_choice`, several calls per
  reply, and `role: "tool"` results on the following turn. This is what
  agent platforms drive their loop with — without it Hermes Agent and thclaws
  could chat but never act.
- **Per-platform setup notes** in the README for Hermes Agent.

- Models `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-sol`, and `gpt-6-luna`, which Matthew added
  in October 2026.
- **`POST /v1/images/generations`** on the standalone server. It returns an
  OpenAI image response with a URL, or base64 with `response_format:
  "b64_json"`. Matthew generates the image in a chat thread, so the assistant
  needs image generation turned on.

### Fixed

- Streaming chat never finished when Matthew sent usage events after the
  reply. The stream stalled, so clients waited forever. The `pull` handler
  now keeps reading until it has output, and event names carry across chunks.
- `content` sent as a list of parts (`[{type: "text", ...}]`) reached
  Matthew as `[object Object]`. Clients switch to that shape once tool
  messages are in play, so it broke the same platforms tool calling is for.
- `role: "tool"` messages were labelled "Instructions" in the transcript
  and assistant `tool_calls` were dropped, so a tool result arrived
  unattributed and the model could not see the call it answered.

## 0.2.0

OpenMatthew started as an OpenCode plugin. It now works with any tool that
speaks the OpenAI API, and OpenCode is one client among several.

### Added

- **A standalone server** (`npm run serve`, or the `openmatthew-serve` bin).
  Speaks `POST /v1/chat/completions` with streaming and non-streaming, so
  any platform with a custom OpenAI base URL setting can use a CMU Matthew
  account without needing a Matthew-specific plugin.
- **`npm run creds`**, which turns the `localStorage.user` blob you copy out
  of Matthew into a ready-to-use bearer token. Previously this meant
  renaming JSON fields and base64-encoding them by hand.
- **`GET /v1/models`**, unauthenticated, because many clients enumerate
  models before you've entered a key and show an empty picker without it.
- **CORS and preflight handling**, without which browser-based platform UIs
  fail before reaching the server.
- **`npm run check-api`**, a drift check that reads Matthew's frontend
  bundle and reports which of our assumptions about its undocumented API no
  longer hold.
- **A test suite.** 17 tests covering the message transform, ticket
  authentication, response envelope, CORS, and error paths, against a fake
  Matthew that enforces the real protocol. There were no tests before, and
  `npm test` matched no files.
- Three models Matthew had added since the last release: `gpt-5.5`,
  `gpt-5.4`, and `gpt-5.4-mini`.
- **Token usage tracking and budget warnings** for the OpenCode plugin.
  OpenCode's panel shows `0 tokens` for Matthew because Matthew strips the
  `usage` field from its stream, so the plugin records usage itself, keeps a
  running total in `~/.config/opencode/matthew-usage.json`, prints it with
  `npm run usage`, and warns when you pass 80% of your dashboard quota.
  Ships alongside token estimation, pre-flight size warnings, and an
  optional system-prompt override (`MATTHEW_SYSTEM_PROMPT`,
  `MATTHEW_OVERRIDE_SYSTEM`).

### Fixed

- **Reading replies was broken.** Matthew changed
  `/api/thread_sse_response_stream` to require a short-lived ticket from
  `/api/thread_sse_ticket` and stopped accepting the access token. Sending a
  message still worked, so messages were charged against your quota and the
  reply never came back. This affected the OpenCode plugin too.
- **System prompts and conversation history were discarded.** Only the last
  user message reached Matthew, so multi-turn conversations lost their
  context and agent instructions were dropped outright.
- **Responses were missing the `id`, `object`, and `created` fields.** The
  OpenAI SDKs validate these and reject payloads without them.
- Stream failures reported "Failed to connect to Matthew SSE" and swallowed
  the status and body. They now include what Matthew actually said, and a
  401 says your session expired.

### Changed

- The OpenCode plugin registers its models through the shared core list, so
  the two can no longer drift apart.
- Matthew's protocol and account storage moved to `src/core/`, which has no
  OpenCode dependency. The plugin is now a thin adapter over it.
- The README leads with the universal path and documents that **the model
  you request is ignored**: Matthew resolves the model from your assistant,
  and its chat API has no model field.

### Removed

- `src/plugin/server.ts`, a local OAuth callback listener that nothing
  imported. Azure AD rejects `localhost` as a redirect URI, so the flow it
  implemented could never run.
- `authorizeMicrosoft` and `exchangeViaMatthew`, along with the Azure AD
  constants they used. They described an authorization-code flow this
  project does not perform, and nothing called them. **Breaking** if you
  imported them directly, though they never worked.
- The `MATTHEW_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` environment variable from the docs. It was
  never read.

## 0.1.0

Initial release. OpenCode plugin for CMU Matthew AI authentication.
